title: Naturality of uncurried tensor-Hom exchange in a braided category
statement:
Let C be any braided monoidal category, M,P,I,Q,Q' objects, e:M tensor P to I a morphism and g:Q to Q' a morphism. Write
$$c_Q=\alpha_{M,Q,P};(1_M\otimes\beta_{Q,P});\alpha^{-1}_{M,P,Q};(e\otimes1_Q): (M\otimes Q)\otimes P\longrightarrow I\otimes Q.$$
Then
$$((1_M\otimes g)\otimes1_P);c_{Q'}=c_Q;(1_I\otimes g).$$
Here semicolons denote composition from left to right, alpha is the associator and beta is the braiding. No symmetry, closedness, additive structure or hypotheses on the objects are required.

source.place: paragraph 1: naturality of the finite-free Hom construction; categorical associator, braiding and tensor interchange identities

proof.text: Apply naturality of the associator in its middle argument to move g across the first associator. Functoriality of left tensoring and left naturality of the braiding move it across the middle braiding. Naturality of the inverse associator in its right argument moves it across the inverse associator. The tensor interchange identity then commutes g with e on the other factor. Reassociate the compositions; the resulting equality is the displayed equation.

lean.statement:
theorem braidedTensorExchange_naturality {V : Type a₀} [Category.{b₀} V]
    [MonoidalCategory V] [BraidedCategory V]
    (M P I Q Q' : V) (ev : M ⊗ P ⟶ I) (g : Q ⟶ Q') :
    ((M ◁ g) ▷ P) ≫ (α_ M Q' P).hom ≫ M ◁ (β_ Q' P).hom ≫
        (α_ M P Q').inv ≫ ev ▷ Q' =
      (α_ M Q P).hom ≫ M ◁ (β_ Q P).hom ≫
        (α_ M P Q).inv ≫ ev ▷ Q ≫ I ◁ g
